stories.title: A Tiny Seed
paragraphs: A Tiny Seed: The Story of Wangari Maathai Nicola Rijsdijk Maya Marshak English Level
In a village on the slopes of Mount Kenya in East Africa, a little girl worked in the fields with her mother. Her name was Wangari.
Wangari loved being outside. In her family’s food garden she broke up the soil with her machete. She pressed tiny seeds into the warm earth.

Her favourite time of day was just after sunset. When it got too dark to see the plants, Wangari knew it was time to go home. She would follow the narrow paths through the fields, crossing rivers as she went.

Wangari was a clever child and couldn’t wait to go to school. But her mother and father wanted her to stay and help them at home. When she was seven years old, her big brother persuaded her parents to let her go to school.

She liked to learn! Wangari learnt more and more with every book she read. She did so well at school that she was invited to study in the United States of America. Wangari was excited! She wanted to know more about the world.

At the American university Wangari learnt many new things. She studied plants and how they grow. And she remembered how she grew: playing games with her brothers in the shade of the trees in the beautiful Kenyan forests.
The more she learnt, the more she realised that she loved the people of Kenya. She wanted them to be happy and free. The more she learnt, the more she remembered her African home.

When she had finished her studies, she returned to Kenya. But her country had changed. Huge farms stretched across the land. Women had no wood to make cooking fires. The people were poor and the children were hungry.

Wangari knew what to do. She taught the women how to plant trees from seeds. The women sold the trees and used the money to look after their families. The women were very happy. Wangari had helped them to feel powerful and strong.
As time passed, the new trees grew into forests, and the rivers started flowing again. Wangari’s message spread across Africa. Today, millions of trees have grown from Wangari’s seeds.
Wangari had worked hard. People all over the world took notice, and gave her a famous prize. It is called the Nobel Peace Prize, and she was the first African woman ever to receive it.
Wangari died in 2011, but we can think of her every time we see a beautiful tree.

stories.title: Paplu, the Giant
stories.synopsis: 不愿打架的巨人，怎样保护他珍惜的人？
paragraphs: This is the story of a nine-year old giant called Paplu. He was very different from the other giants. They loved to fight, whereas Paplu hated fighting.
While his classmates would spend their time twisting the ears of dinosaurs or yanking the tails of tigers, Paplu would be busy protecting his friends. Paplu’s mother was worried about her son.
One night she woke up Paplu. “Son, you will never be happy staying in our tribe. I am taking you to a village where people are normal human beings. You will stay there with Raghav, the head man.”
Just before they reached the village, Paplu’s mother asked him to close his eyes. When he opened them, he almost fainted.
He had shrunk to one-tenth his size and so had she. Paplu’s mother handed him over to Raghav and left.
Paplu soon made friends with the boys and girls of the village. One day Raghav came home very worried. “A ruthless bandit called Angaar has blocked the only way out of our village.
We cannot go to our farms to work and will surely starve,” he said. Paplu wished he could help Raghav in some way. Paplu suddenly remembered something.
Before leaving the forest, his mother had told him the magic words which would make him a giant once again. And as a giant, he would easily be able to take care of Angaar.
Paplu did everything he could, including standing on his head and pulling his own ears, but he couldn’t remember those words.
Then Paplu heard a soft lisp. “Paplu paiyaa, play with me, pleath.” It was his two-year old neighbour Soni. Paplu was her best friend.
He picked her up and threw her high in the air and she started singing: “Paplu paiyya, Paplu paiyaa thlow me up, cath me quick, Paplu paiyya, Paplu paiyya please show me youll magic thlik.”
Paplu froze! These words and the tune sounded very familiar. He rushed inside and came out with a blue stone in his hand.
He now remembered what his mother had told him, “Son, throw the stone in the air and say these words: I’ll throw you up, I’ll catch you quick. Don’t forget my magic trick.”
As Paplu threw the stone and recited the words, he felt himself swelling up like a balloon. Suddenly he heard a sound – R-r-rip! R-ri-ip!! His clothes were tearing.
If he didn’t look for cover, he would soon be standing bang in the middle of the village, in clothes hundred sizes too small for him.

All he would have to cover his modesty would be strips of cloth and little else. Paplu rushed into the woods with the sound ‘R-r-rip! Rri-i-p!’ chasing him. Once deep into the undergrowth, Paplu got down on his knees.
It looked like he had missed a word or two in the magic chant his mother had made him learn.
That is why his clothes had not grown along with his body!

What was he to do now? Although he had become a giant, he couldn’t venture out on his rescue mission in his birthday suit. He needed clothes urgently. But how was he to get clothes his size and that too, quickly?
He heard a voice and looked down. It was Raghav.
“Soni told me you had become big and that you had run away somewhere. When I heard this strange story, I came out to investigate.” “Using a magic trick my mother taught me, I have become a giant.
Now I can take care of Angaar and his gang,” said Paplu. “That’s great, then what are you waiting for?”

“My clothes didn’t keep pace with my growth. I am wearing almost nothing. How can I come out like this?” Raghav thought for some time and said, “Okay, give me some time. By nightfall, I’ll have your clothes ready.”

Raghav went back home and summoned all the tailors in the village. Twenty one tailors appeared in no time. Raghav explained the problem to them and said, “I want a pair of pyjamas and a kurta, to be stitched as soon as possible for Paplu.”
Soon ‘Operation Paplu Dress’ started.

It was quite funny to see the tailors scrambling up Paplu’s back, legs and hands to take his measurements. The whole village got into action contributing whatever material they could. Even Soni donated her doll’s shawl to the project!
In seven hours, the dress was ready.

In seven hours, with a whoop of joy, Paplu stood up towering over the villagers. He looked really smart with the multi- coloured kurta and an equally multi-coloured pyjama. There was thunderous applause.
It was just past midnight. Angaar and his men were fast asleep. Only two bandits were on guard. Suddenly Angaar woke up. He could hear a strange sound.
He got up and picking up his sword, rushed out of his tent. The other dacoits too were coming out of their enclosures, spears and swords in hand. “Whoosh!”
There was the sound again. It seemed to be growing louder and closer. “WHOOSH!” Angaar looked around. A dust storm seemed to be gathering momentum.

Trees had started swaying and the noise was slowly becoming deafening. “WHOOSH! WHOOSH!” Angaar felt himself being picked up by the air current. He desperately tried to hold on, flaying his arms and legs, but it was no use.
He was flying in the air. To his left, was his deputy Jarnail looking like an ungainly dinosaur.

To his right, was his most accomplished swordsman, Talwar, air-borne like his colleagues, desperately trying to reach out for his sword which was flying ahead of him. A few minutes later, there was a splash.

They landed in the river to the south of the village. As they swam to the shore, spluttering and shivering, a huge shadow loomed over their heads. “Angaar, you scoundrel!” the shadow thundered, its voice echoing in the night.
“Y … yes,” stammered the dreaded Angaar.
He had never been so terrified in his life, since the day his father, Rosh Bundela had walloped him for eating up his jalebis. “This time I have merely roughed you up.
Next time, if you or any of your men come anywhere close to the village, I’ll rip each and every limb from your bodies and chew them up.”
“Y..yes, Maharaj, we will never again come within a thousand miles of this place.”
“Good. Remember, if I hear you are even passing through these parts, I’ll make a paste of you and your gang and feed it to the fish in this river.” “Yes, Maharaj. But please, do tell me, who are you?
I have never seen you in these parts.” “I am a guardian of this village,” Paplu said.

He paused for a good ten seconds and then in his deepest tone said, “And my name is Paplu, the Giant.” And with these words, Paplu stormed back to the village. Angaar and his men left the same night and were never heard of again.
Paplu went back to his original shape and size.
However, he couldn’t get back his original name. No one called him Paplu anymore. To everyone, and even to Soni, he was Paplu, the Giant.

sentences.zh: 他所需要的只是布条，除此之外别无他物。

sentences.zh: 帕普卢冲进树林，发出“R-r-rip！”的声音。

sentences.zh: “Rri-i-p！”追着他。

sentences.zh: 看起来他错过了母亲让他学的魔法咒语中的一两个单词。

sentences.zh: 所以他的衣服并没有随着身体一起长大！

picturePages.text: What was he to do now? Although he had become a giant, he couldn’t venture out on his rescue mission in his birthday suit. He needed clothes urgently. But how was he to get clothes his size and that too, quickly?

sentences.zh: 他现在该怎么办？

sentences.zh: 虽然他已经变成了巨人，但他却无法穿着生日服冒险去执行救援任务。

sentences.zh: 他急需衣服。

sentences.en: But how was he to get clothes his size and that too, quickly?
sentences.zh: 但他怎样才能快速买到适合自己尺码的衣服呢？

sentences.zh: 他听到一个声音，低下头。

Angaar looked around.
sentences.zh: 安加尔环顾四周。

sentences.zh: 在他的右边，是他最出色的剑客塔尔瓦，他和他的同事一样在空中，拼命地试图伸手去拿在他前面飞过的剑。

sentences.zh: 几分钟后，水花四溅。

sentences.zh: “安加尔，你这个无赖！”

sentences.en: the shadow thundered, its voice echoing in the night.
sentences.zh: 影子发出雷鸣般的声音，它的声音在夜色中回荡。

picturePages.text: “Y … yes,” stammered the dreaded Angaar.

sentences.en: “Y … yes,” stammered the dreaded Angaar.
sentences.zh: “是……是的，”可怕的安加尔结结巴巴地说。

sentences.en: He had never been so terrified in his life, since the day his father, Rosh Bundela had walloped him for eating up his jalebis.
sentences.zh: 自从他的父亲罗什·邦德拉因为他吃掉了贾勒比斯而狠狠地打了他一顿之后，他这辈子从来没有这么害怕过。

sentences.en: “This time I have merely roughed you up.
sentences.zh: “这次我只是粗暴地对待了你而已。

sentences.zh: 下次，如果你或你的任何人来到村庄附近的任何地方，我会把你身上的每一个肢体都撕下来然后咀嚼。”

sentences.en: “Y..yes, Maharaj, we will never again come within a thousand miles of this place.”
sentences.zh: “是的……是的，马哈拉吉，我们再也不会来到距离这个地方一千英里以内的地方了。”

picturePages.text: “Good. Remember, if I hear you are even passing through these parts, I’ll make a paste of you and your gang and feed it to the fish in this river.” “Yes, Maharaj. But please, do tell me, who are you?

sentences.en: “Good.
Remember, if I hear you are even passing through these parts, I’ll make a paste of you and your gang and feed it to the fish in this river.”
sentences.zh: 记住，如果我听说你路过这些地方，我会把你和你的帮派弄成糊状，喂这条河里的鱼。”

sentences.en: “Yes, Maharaj.
sentences.zh: “是的，马哈拉吉。

sentences.en: But please, do tell me, who are you?
sentences.zh: 但请告诉我，你是谁？

picturePages.text: I have never seen you in these parts.” “I am a guardian of this village,” Paplu said.

sentences.en: I have never seen you in these parts.”
sentences.zh: 我从来没有在这些地方见过你。”

sentences.en: “I am a guardian of this village,” Paplu said.
sentences.zh: “我是这个村庄的守护者，”帕普卢说。

picturePages.text: He paused for a good ten seconds and then in his deepest tone said, “And my name is Paplu, the Giant.” And with these words, Paplu stormed back to the village. Angaar and his men left the same night and were never heard of again.

sentences.en: He paused for a good ten seconds and then in his deepest tone said, “And my name is Paplu, the Giant.”
sentences.zh: 他停顿了整整十秒钟，然后用最深沉的语气说道：“我的名字是巨人帕普卢。”

sentences.en: And with these words, Paplu stormed back to the village.
sentences.zh: 说完这句话，帕普鲁怒气冲冲地回了村子。

sentences.en: Angaar and his men left the same night and were never heard of again.
sentences.zh: 安加尔和他的部下于当晚离开，从此杳无音讯。

picturePages.text: Paplu went back to his original shape and size.

sentences.en: Paplu went back to his original shape and size.
sentences.zh: 帕普鲁又恢复了原来的形状和大小。

picturePages.text: However, he couldn’t get back his original name. No one called him Paplu anymore. To everyone, and even to Soni, he was Paplu, the Giant.

sentences.zh: 然而，他却无法找回自己原来的名字。

sentences.en: No one called him Paplu anymore.
sentences.zh: 没有人再叫他帕普鲁了。

sentences.en: To everyone, and even to Soni, he was Paplu, the Giant.
sentences.zh: 对于每个人，甚至对于索尼来说，他都是巨人帕普鲁。

stories.title: The Elephant Bird
stories.synopsis: 马失踪了，所有人都怀疑巨鸟。一个女孩决定寻找真相。
paragraphs: Munia knew that the giant, one-feathered elephant bird had not swallowed the horse. Yes, he was big enough to swallow a horse, but that didn't mean he had! The village of Adhania had only one horse-cart pulled by the two horses Vayu and Drut.
And Vayu had gone missing near the lake in the jungle where the bird lived.
The villagers had known about the elephant bird for generations.

He was the last of his race, which was considered extinct for hundreds of years. The world did not know that the living relic of that race, who had lost all his feathers but one, still roamed the jungles of Adhania.
The bird and the villagers kept a safe distance from each other. But not Munia.
Although she walked with a limp, she was brave of heart. She often slipped into the jungle to watch the elephant bird.
The elephant bird came near the lake in the daytime to bask in the sun or play in the lake alone splashing water. Sometimes he sat half-submerged in water. At other times there was no trace of him.
Perhaps he just rested in some corner of the dense jungle. He stood as tall as a tree.
He had a long strong neck, huge legs with claws and a heavy spear-like head. His long talons and nails looked scary.

But Munia soon realised he was a shy herbivorous bird. He just munched on leaves by the lakeside. Munia felt she had something in common with him. The elephant bird could not fly and Munia could not run!
Other village children mocked her limp and did not include her in their games. That was why she liked staying alone.

Every morning Munia helped fetch three pitchers of water from the village well, and collected wood so that Amma could light the stove. And then she would be out for a long time. Amma believed she went out to play with the kids.
Little did she know that Munia went into the jungle to the lake where the elephant bird lived.
One day, gathering courage, Munia stepped in the open near the lake. Without turning his head the elephant bird rolled his eyes towards Munia and then closed them, uninterested by her advance.
Getting no more attention than the flies buzzing over his head, Munia stomped her feet. Suddenly the elephant bird lifted one of his claws.
Munia cried and fell headlong into the shallow waters of the lake. She came out drenched to see him shaking all over. He was laughing!

“That’s funny, huh?” she asked angrily and turned to leave. Before Munia had walked away from the clearing, something hit her feet. It was a fruit that the elephant bird had thrown at her. The elephant bird wanted to play!
Hesitantly, Munia threw it at him. He trotted sideways and caught the fruit in his beak.
Thus, Munia’s friendship with the elephant bird had begun. And just when she had finally found a friend, Vayu had gone missing! And everyone’s suspicion had turned towards the elephant bird.

After searching for Vayu high and low, the villagers gathered under the old banyan tree. Everyone agreed that there could be no thief in Adhania. They all trusted one another. The milkman swore that he had seen Vayu gallop away towards the lake.
“There is no sign of Vayu anywhere.

It must be something in the jungle that got him,” a villager addressed the headman. “Who else can it be but the giant one-feathered elephant bird? He must be destroyed!” said the milkman. “For years he has been lying silent, hatching his evil plans!”

The crowd agreed. Munia watched the proceedings quietly. She wanted to speak, but was scared of being punished for speaking up. Even if she spoke, who would believe her? “Yes, all these years of aimless living has made the giant dangerous,” said Munia’s father.

“Today it is a horse, tomorrow it may be our children … ” The headman spoke over the villagers’ angry shouts, “Brothers, even though we are facing a giant, we have the strength of numbers. So let us go out and finish him!”

A cheer of approval went up. “The elephant bird did not eat the horse,” Munia said softly but firmly, limping forward. “I was with him when Vayu went missing!” A heavy silence fell on the gathering. “What does this mean?”
roared the headman. “That the elephant bird is my friend, and he has not done this!”
“This girl has lost her mind!” shouted someone from the back. The other children laughed. “He only eats leaves! How can he eat Vayu?”
Munia shouted, not moving from her place.

“You can’t even plait your hair and you are giving us advice?” Munia’s father fumed and came towards her. “Go play with your friends!” “This elephant bird is the only friend I have,” said Munia. Her father glared at her.
But she didn’t cry and stood there facing the villagers.
“Forget about the girl, we will get the elephant bird in the morning,” said the headman and the gathering dispersed.
Munia had only one night to prove the elephant bird’s innocence. “Think, Munia, think!” she whispered to herself. “The milkman saw Vayu gallop away on the road that goes to the lake.
But the road takes a turn before it reaches the lake and goes towards Chandesara. What if Vayu had gone that way?”
Munia’s parents were angry with her and sent her to bed without speaking a word. Once they were asleep, she got out of bed, took the hanging lamp and stepped out of the house.

She crossed Adhania, and came to the jungle path leading to Chandesara, the neighbouring village. Whoooo... rang the call of an owl in the jungle air. A jackal howled from a distance. The shadows of trees moved like long dark fingers.
She hesitated for a moment but then thought of the elephant bird sleeping peacefully in the jungle.
If she didn't do something to solve the mystery, the elephant bird may not be alive to see the next night. She took a deep breath and limped alone on the jungle path in the dead of the night.

The next morning the villagers gathered near the lake with sticks, sharp stones and long kitchen knives. The elephant bird was resting when the crowd approached him. The sun shone on his featherless back. He got up slowly and stared at the crowd.
Looking at his size, the villagers stopped at some distance.
After a moment’s hesitation the headman cried, “Be ready!” The mob roared, firming the grip on the weapons, ready to run down the giant one-feathered elephant bird.
“Stop!” Munia’s thin voice cut through the din. She limped between the mob and the giant. “Munia! Come back at once!”
her father ordered. “Grab her!” cried someone else. Munia’s father and another villager rushed towards her. The elephant bird advanced a couple of steps and they stopped.
“Okay … if this is how you want it, we’ll tackle both of you together!” yelled a man, holding a spear.

“What’s going on?” someone shouted from behind the crowd. A slightly hunched man with a long beard came in holding a horse’s reins. The headman asked with a surprised look, “Saarthi, what are you doing here? And why is Vayu with you?”
“Oh, as you know, I had sold Vayu to you some years back. Yesterday I was passing by your village early in the morning in my buggy pulled by Jhabru and Ghabru – Vayu’s brothers.
I don’t know how Vayu got loose and followed us back to Chandesara!
I couldn’t recognize him and didn’t know what to do with him until this morning when I saw this little girl going from hut to hut, asking about a lost horse. But what is going on?” he asked again.

The villagers did not answer Saarthi. They hung their heads in shame. Munia’s father went to her, lifted her in his arms and took her back to the village. Since that day, no child laughed at Munia’s limp.
They all wanted to be friends with her. And they all wanted to be friends with the elephant bird.
Munia’s tale reached many villages and the villagers in faraway hamlets whispered to each other, “Munia knew that the giant one-feathered elephant bird had not swallowed the horse!”

This story is inspired by the real Elephant Bird (scientific name: Aepyornis maximus), the biggest bird that walked our planet. It inhabited the island of Madagascar. With more and more settlements on the island, and more forests ruined, the species became extinct around 1700 CE.

sentences.zh: 他是他的种族的最后一个，这个种族被认为已经灭绝了数百年。

sentences.en: The world did not know that the living relic of that race, who had lost all his feathers but one, still roamed the jungles of Adhania.
sentences.zh: 世人并不知道，这个种族的活遗物，除了一根羽毛之外，已经失去了所有羽毛，仍然在阿达尼亚的丛林中漫步。

picturePages.text: The bird and the villagers kept a safe distance from each other. But not Munia.

sentences.en: The bird and the villagers kept a safe distance from each other.
sentences.zh: 这只鸟和村民们彼此保持着安全距离。

sentences.en: But not Munia.
sentences.zh: 但穆尼亚则不然。

picturePages.text: Although she walked with a limp, she was brave of heart. She often slipped into the jungle to watch the elephant bird.

sentences.en: Although she walked with a limp, she was brave of heart.
sentences.zh: 尽管她走路一瘸一拐，但她的内心却很勇敢。

sentences.en: She often slipped into the jungle to watch the elephant bird.
sentences.zh: 她经常溜进丛林观察象鸟。

picturePages.text: The elephant bird came near the lake in the daytime to bask in the sun or play in the lake alone splashing water. Sometimes he sat half-submerged in water. At other times there was no trace of him.

sentences.en: The elephant bird came near the lake in the daytime to bask in the sun or play in the lake alone splashing water.
sentences.zh: 象鸟白天来到湖边晒太阳，或者独自在湖里戏水。

sentences.en: Sometimes he sat half-submerged in water.
sentences.zh: 有时他半浸在水里。

sentences.en: At other times there was no trace of him.
sentences.zh: 其他时候都没有他的踪迹。

picturePages.text: Perhaps he just rested in some corner of the dense jungle. He stood as tall as a tree.

sentences.en: Perhaps he just rested in some corner of the dense jungle.
sentences.zh: 也许他只是在茂密丛林的某个角落休息。

sentences.en: He stood as tall as a tree.
sentences.zh: 他站得像一棵树一样高。

picturePages.text: He had a long strong neck, huge legs with claws and a heavy spear-like head. His long talons and nails looked scary.

sentences.en: He had a long strong neck, huge legs with claws and a heavy spear-like head.
sentences.zh: 他有一个又长又粗的脖子，长着爪子的巨大腿和一个像矛一样沉重的头。

sentences.en: His long talons and nails looked scary.
sentences.zh: 他的长爪子和指甲看起来很吓人。

picturePages.text: But Munia soon realised he was a shy herbivorous bird. He just munched on leaves by the lakeside. Munia felt she had something in common with him. The elephant bird could not fly and Munia could not run!

sentences.en: But Munia soon realised he was a shy herbivorous bird.
sentences.zh: 但穆尼亚很快意识到他是一只害羞的草食鸟。

sentences.en: He just munched on leaves by the lakeside.
sentences.zh: 他只是在湖边嚼着树叶。

sentences.en: Munia felt she had something in common with him.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚觉得她和他有一些共同点。

sentences.en: The elephant bird could not fly and Munia could not run!
sentences.zh: 象鸟不会飞，文尼亚也不会跑！

picturePages.text: Other village children mocked her limp and did not include her in their games. That was why she liked staying alone.

sentences.en: Other village children mocked her limp and did not include her in their games.
sentences.zh: 其他村里的孩子嘲笑她跛行，不让她参加他们的游戏。

sentences.en: That was why she liked staying alone.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么她喜欢一个人待着。

picturePages.text: Every morning Munia helped fetch three pitchers of water from the village well, and collected wood so that Amma could light the stove. And then she would be out for a long time. Amma believed she went out to play with the kids.

sentences.en: Every morning Munia helped fetch three pitchers of water from the village well, and collected wood so that Amma could light the stove.
sentences.zh: 每天早上，穆尼亚都会帮忙从村里的井里打三壶水，并收集木材，以便阿玛可以生火炉。

sentences.en: And then she would be out for a long time.
sentences.zh: 然后她就会出去很长一段时间。

sentences.en: Amma believed she went out to play with the kids.
sentences.zh: 阿妈相信她是出去和孩子们玩的。

picturePages.text: Little did she know that Munia went into the jungle to the lake where the elephant bird lived.

sentences.en: Little did she know that Munia went into the jungle to the lake where the elephant bird lived.
sentences.zh: 她不知道穆尼亚走进了丛林，来到了象鸟居住的湖边。

picturePages.text: One day, gathering courage, Munia stepped in the open near the lake. Without turning his head the elephant bird rolled his eyes towards Munia and then closed them, uninterested by her advance.

sentences.en: One day, gathering courage, Munia stepped in the open near the lake.
sentences.zh: 有一天，穆尼亚鼓起勇气，踏入了湖边的空地。

sentences.en: Without turning his head the elephant bird rolled his eyes towards Munia and then closed them, uninterested by her advance.
sentences.zh: 象鸟头也不回地朝穆尼亚翻了个白眼，然后闭上了眼睛，对她的举动不感兴趣。

picturePages.text: Getting no more attention than the flies buzzing over his head, Munia stomped her feet. Suddenly the elephant bird lifted one of his claws.

sentences.en: Getting no more attention than the flies buzzing over his head, Munia stomped her feet.
sentences.zh: 穆妮亚跺着脚，就像头顶上嗡嗡作响的苍蝇一样，没有受到更多的关注。

sentences.en: Suddenly the elephant bird lifted one of his claws.
sentences.zh: 突然，象鸟举起了一只爪子。

picturePages.text: Munia cried and fell headlong into the shallow waters of the lake. She came out drenched to see him shaking all over. He was laughing!

sentences.en: Munia cried and fell headlong into the shallow waters of the lake.
sentences.zh: 文尼亚哭着，一头栽进了湖的浅水里。

sentences.en: She came out drenched to see him shaking all over.
sentences.zh: 她浑身湿透地出来，看到他浑身发抖。

sentences.en: He was laughing!
sentences.zh: 他在笑！

picturePages.text: “That’s funny, huh?” she asked angrily and turned to leave. Before Munia had walked away from the clearing, something hit her feet. It was a fruit that the elephant bird had thrown at her. The elephant bird wanted to play!

sentences.en: “That’s funny, huh?”
sentences.zh: “这很有趣，是吧？”

sentences.en: she asked angrily and turned to leave.
sentences.zh: 她愤怒地问道，转身就走。

sentences.en: Before Munia had walked away from the clearing, something hit her feet.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚还没走出空地，就有什么东西撞到了她的脚上。

sentences.en: It was a fruit that the elephant bird had thrown at her.
sentences.zh: 那是象鸟扔给她的果实。

sentences.en: The elephant bird wanted to play!
sentences.zh: 象鸟想玩！

picturePages.text: Hesitantly, Munia threw it at him. He trotted sideways and caught the fruit in his beak.

sentences.en: Hesitantly, Munia threw it at him.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚犹豫了一下，把它扔给了他。

sentences.en: He trotted sideways and caught the fruit in his beak.
sentences.zh: 他侧身小跑，用嘴叼住了水果。

picturePages.text: Thus, Munia’s friendship with the elephant bird had begun. And just when she had finally found a friend, Vayu had gone missing! And everyone’s suspicion had turned towards the elephant bird.

sentences.en: Thus, Munia’s friendship with the elephant bird had begun.
sentences.zh: 就这样，文尼亚与象鸟的友谊开始了。

sentences.en: And just when she had finally found a friend, Vayu had gone missing!
sentences.zh: 就在她终于找到朋友的时候，Vayu却失踪了！

sentences.en: And everyone’s suspicion had turned towards the elephant bird.
sentences.zh: 而所有人的怀疑，都转向了象鸟。

picturePages.text: After searching for Vayu high and low, the villagers gathered under the old banyan tree. Everyone agreed that there could be no thief in Adhania. They all trusted one another. The milkman swore that he had seen Vayu gallop away towards the lake.

sentences.en: After searching for Vayu high and low, the villagers gathered under the old banyan tree.
sentences.zh: 上下寻找瓦尤后，村民们聚集在老榕树下。

sentences.en: Everyone agreed that there could be no thief in Adhania.
sentences.zh: 大家一致认为，阿达尼亚不可能有小偷。

sentences.en: They all trusted one another.
sentences.zh: 他们都互相信任。

sentences.en: The milkman swore that he had seen Vayu gallop away towards the lake.
sentences.zh: 送牛奶的人发誓他看到瓦尤向湖边疾驰而去。

picturePages.text: “There is no sign of Vayu anywhere.

sentences.en: “There is no sign of Vayu anywhere.
sentences.zh: “到处都没有瓦尤的迹象。

picturePages.text: It must be something in the jungle that got him,” a villager addressed the headman. “Who else can it be but the giant one-feathered elephant bird? He must be destroyed!” said the milkman. “For years he has been lying silent, hatching his evil plans!”

sentences.en: It must be something in the jungle that got him,” a villager addressed the headman.
sentences.zh: 一定是丛林里的什么东西把他抓走了。”一位村民对村长说道。

sentences.en: “Who else can it be but the giant one-feathered elephant bird?
sentences.zh: “除了那只巨大的单羽象鸟还能是谁？

sentences.en: He must be destroyed!”
sentences.zh: 必须消灭他！”

sentences.en: said the milkman.
sentences.zh: 送奶工说。

sentences.en: “For years he has been lying silent, hatching his evil plans!”
sentences.zh: “多年来他一直沉默不语，酝酿着他的邪恶计划！”

picturePages.text: The crowd agreed. Munia watched the proceedings quietly. She wanted to speak, but was scared of being punished for speaking up. Even if she spoke, who would believe her? “Yes, all these years of aimless living has made the giant dangerous,” said Munia’s father.

sentences.en: The crowd agreed.
sentences.zh: 众人纷纷表示同意。

sentences.en: Munia watched the proceedings quietly.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚静静地观看着整个过程。

sentences.en: She wanted to speak, but was scared of being punished for speaking up.
sentences.zh: 她想说话，但又害怕说话会受到惩罚。

sentences.en: Even if she spoke, who would believe her?
sentences.zh: 就算她说出来，又有谁会相信呢？

sentences.en: “Yes, all these years of aimless living has made the giant dangerous,” said Munia’s father.
sentences.zh: “是的，这些年漫无目的的生活让巨人变得危险，”穆尼亚的父亲说。

picturePages.text: “Today it is a horse, tomorrow it may be our children … ” The headman spoke over the villagers’ angry shouts, “Brothers, even though we are facing a giant, we have the strength of numbers. So let us go out and finish him!”

sentences.en: “Today it is a horse, tomorrow it may be our children … ” The headman spoke over the villagers’ angry shouts, “Brothers, even though we are facing a giant, we have the strength of numbers.
sentences.zh: “今天是一匹马，明天可能就是我们的孩子……”村长在村民们的愤怒叫喊中说道，“兄弟们，虽然我们面对的是巨人，但我们人多力量大。

sentences.en: So let us go out and finish him!”
sentences.zh: 那我们就出去干掉他吧！”

picturePages.text: A cheer of approval went up. “The elephant bird did not eat the horse,” Munia said softly but firmly, limping forward. “I was with him when Vayu went missing!” A heavy silence fell on the gathering. “What does this mean?”

sentences.en: A cheer of approval went up.
sentences.zh: 一阵赞同的欢呼声响起。

sentences.en: “The elephant bird did not eat the horse,” Munia said softly but firmly, limping forward.
sentences.zh: “象鸟没有吃掉马。”穆尼亚一瘸一拐地向前走，轻声但坚定地说。

sentences.en: “I was with him when Vayu went missing!”
sentences.zh: “Vayu失踪时我就在他身边！”

sentences.en: A heavy silence fell on the gathering.
sentences.zh: 会场陷入一片沉静。

sentences.en: “What does this mean?”
sentences.zh: “这是什么意思？”

picturePages.text: roared the headman. “That the elephant bird is my friend, and he has not done this!”

sentences.en: roared the headman.
sentences.zh: 村长咆哮道。

sentences.en: “That the elephant bird is my friend, and he has not done this!”
sentences.zh: “象鸟是我的朋友，他没有这么做！”

picturePages.text: “This girl has lost her mind!” shouted someone from the back. The other children laughed. “He only eats leaves! How can he eat Vayu?”

sentences.en: “This girl has lost her mind!”
sentences.zh: “这丫头疯了！”

sentences.en: shouted someone from the back.
sentences.zh: 后面有人喊道。

sentences.en: The other children laughed.
sentences.zh: 其他孩子都笑了。

sentences.en: “He only eats leaves!
sentences.zh: “他只吃叶子！

sentences.en: How can he eat Vayu?”
sentences.zh: 他怎么能吃Vayu呢？”

picturePages.text: Munia shouted, not moving from her place.

sentences.en: Munia shouted, not moving from her place.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚大喊道，没有离开自己的位置。

picturePages.text: “You can’t even plait your hair and you are giving us advice?” Munia’s father fumed and came towards her. “Go play with your friends!” “This elephant bird is the only friend I have,” said Munia. Her father glared at her.

sentences.en: “You can’t even plait your hair and you are giving us advice?”
sentences.zh: “你连头发都不会编，还给我们提建议？”

sentences.en: Munia’s father fumed and came towards her.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚的父亲勃然大怒，朝她走来。

sentences.en: “Go play with your friends!”
sentences.zh: “和你的朋友一起去玩吧！”

sentences.en: “This elephant bird is the only friend I have,” said Munia.
sentences.zh: “这只象鸟是我唯一的朋友，”穆尼亚说。

sentences.en: Her father glared at her.
sentences.zh: 她父亲瞪了她一眼。

picturePages.text: But she didn’t cry and stood there facing the villagers.

sentences.en: But she didn’t cry and stood there facing the villagers.
sentences.zh: 但她没有哭，面向村民站在那里。

picturePages.text: “Forget about the girl, we will get the elephant bird in the morning,” said the headman and the gathering dispersed.

sentences.en: “Forget about the girl, we will get the elephant bird in the morning,” said the headman and the gathering dispersed.
sentences.zh: “别管那个女孩了，我们明天早上就能得到象鸟。”头领说道，人群散去。

picturePages.text: Munia had only one night to prove the elephant bird’s innocence. “Think, Munia, think!” she whispered to herself. “The milkman saw Vayu gallop away on the road that goes to the lake.

sentences.en: Munia had only one night to prove the elephant bird’s innocence.
sentences.zh: 文尼亚只有一个晚上的时间来证明象鸟的清白。

sentences.en: “Think, Munia, think!”
sentences.zh: “想一想，穆尼亚，想一想！”

sentences.en: she whispered to herself.
sentences.zh: 她自言自语道。

sentences.en: “The milkman saw Vayu gallop away on the road that goes to the lake.
sentences.zh: “送奶工看到瓦尤在通往湖边的路上疾驰而去。

picturePages.text: But the road takes a turn before it reaches the lake and goes towards Chandesara. What if Vayu had gone that way?”

sentences.en: But the road takes a turn before it reaches the lake and goes towards Chandesara.
sentences.zh: 但道路在到达湖边之前拐了一个弯，通向钱德萨拉。

sentences.en: What if Vayu had gone that way?”
sentences.zh: 如果 Vayu 走了那条路怎么办？”

picturePages.text: Munia’s parents were angry with her and sent her to bed without speaking a word. Once they were asleep, she got out of bed, took the hanging lamp and stepped out of the house.

sentences.en: Munia’s parents were angry with her and sent her to bed without speaking a word.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚的父母对她很生气，二话不说就把她送上床睡觉。

sentences.en: Once they were asleep, she got out of bed, took the hanging lamp and stepped out of the house.
sentences.zh: 等他们睡着了，她就下了床，拿着吊灯走出了屋子。

picturePages.text: She crossed Adhania, and came to the jungle path leading to Chandesara, the neighbouring village. Whoooo... rang the call of an owl in the jungle air. A jackal howled from a distance. The shadows of trees moved like long dark fingers.

sentences.en: She crossed Adhania, and came to the jungle path leading to Chandesara, the neighbouring village.
sentences.zh: 她穿过阿达尼亚，来到通往邻村钱德萨拉的丛林小道。

sentences.en: Whoooo... rang the call of an owl in the jungle air.
sentences.zh: 呼……丛林中传来猫头鹰的叫声。

sentences.en: A jackal howled from a distance.
sentences.zh: 远处传来豺狼的嚎叫声。

sentences.en: The shadows of trees moved like long dark fingers.
sentences.zh: 树影像又长又黑的手指一样移动。

picturePages.text: She hesitated for a moment but then thought of the elephant bird sleeping peacefully in the jungle.

sentences.en: She hesitated for a moment but then thought of the elephant bird sleeping peacefully in the jungle.
sentences.zh: 她犹豫了一会儿，然后想到了大象鸟在丛林里安静地睡觉。

picturePages.text: If she didn't do something to solve the mystery, the elephant bird may not be alive to see the next night. She took a deep breath and limped alone on the jungle path in the dead of the night.

sentences.en: If she didn't do something to solve the mystery, the elephant bird may not be alive to see the next night.
sentences.zh: 如果她不采取行动解开这个谜团，象鸟可能就活不到第二天晚上了。

sentences.en: She took a deep breath and limped alone on the jungle path in the dead of the night.
sentences.zh: 她深吸了一口气，夜深人静的时候，独自一瘸一拐地走在丛林小路上。

picturePages.text: The next morning the villagers gathered near the lake with sticks, sharp stones and long kitchen knives. The elephant bird was resting when the crowd approached him. The sun shone on his featherless back. He got up slowly and stared at the crowd.

sentences.en: The next morning the villagers gathered near the lake with sticks, sharp stones and long kitchen knives.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，村民们拿着棍棒、锋利的石头和长菜刀聚集在湖边。

sentences.en: The elephant bird was resting when the crowd approached him.
sentences.zh: 当人群靠近时，象鸟正在休息。

sentences.en: The sun shone on his featherless back.
sentences.zh: 阳光照在他光秃秃的背上。

sentences.en: He got up slowly and stared at the crowd.
sentences.zh: 他缓缓起身，目光看向众人。

picturePages.text: Looking at his size, the villagers stopped at some distance.

sentences.en: Looking at his size, the villagers stopped at some distance.
sentences.zh: 看着他的体型，村民们在远处停了下来。

picturePages.text: After a moment’s hesitation the headman cried, “Be ready!” The mob roared, firming the grip on the weapons, ready to run down the giant one-feathered elephant bird.

sentences.en: After a moment’s hesitation the headman cried, “Be ready!”
sentences.zh: 村长犹豫片刻后喊道：“准备好！”

sentences.en: The mob roared, firming the grip on the weapons, ready to run down the giant one-feathered elephant bird.
sentences.zh: 暴民们咆哮着，握紧了武器，准备冲向那只巨大的单羽象鸟。

picturePages.text: “Stop!” Munia’s thin voice cut through the din. She limped between the mob and the giant. “Munia! Come back at once!”

sentences.en: “Stop!”
sentences.zh: “住手！”

sentences.en: Munia’s thin voice cut through the din.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚微弱的声音划破了喧嚣。

sentences.en: She limped between the mob and the giant.
sentences.zh: 她一瘸一拐地走在暴徒和巨人之间。

sentences.en: “Munia!
sentences.zh: “穆尼亚！

sentences.en: Come back at once!”
sentences.zh: 赶紧回来吧！”

picturePages.text: her father ordered. “Grab her!” cried someone else. Munia’s father and another villager rushed towards her. The elephant bird advanced a couple of steps and they stopped.

sentences.en: her father ordered.
sentences.zh: 她父亲命令道。

sentences.en: “Grab her!”
sentences.zh: “抓住她！”

sentences.en: cried someone else.
sentences.zh: 另一个人喊道。

sentences.en: Munia’s father and another villager rushed towards her.
sentences.zh: 穆尼亚的父亲和另一名村民冲向她。

sentences.en: The elephant bird advanced a couple of steps and they stopped.
sentences.zh: 象鸟向前走了几步，他们停了下来。

picturePages.text: “Okay … if this is how you want it, we’ll tackle both of you together!” yelled a man, holding a spear.

sentences.en: “Okay … if this is how you want it, we’ll tackle both of you together!”
sentences.zh: “好吧……既然你们想要这样，那我们就一起对付你们吧！”

sentences.en: yelled a man, holding a spear.
sentences.zh: 一个拿着长矛的男人喊道。

picturePages.text: “What’s going on?” someone shouted from behind the crowd. A slightly hunched man with a long beard came in holding a horse’s reins. The headman asked with a surprised look, “Saarthi, what are you doing here? And why is Vayu with you?”

sentences.en: “What’s going on?”
sentences.zh: “这是怎么回事？”

sentences.en: someone shouted from behind the crowd.
sentences.zh: 有人在人群后面喊道。

sentences.en: A slightly hunched man with a long beard came in holding a horse’s reins.
sentences.zh: 一个有点驼背、留着长胡子的男人牵着马缰绳走了进来。

sentences.en: The headman asked with a surprised look, “Saarthi, what are you doing here?
sentences.zh: 头领惊讶地问道：“Saarthi，你来这里做什么？

sentences.en: And why is Vayu with you?”
sentences.zh: 为什么 Vayu 会和你在一起？”

picturePages.text: “Oh, as you know, I had sold Vayu to you some years back. Yesterday I was passing by your village early in the morning in my buggy pulled by Jhabru and Ghabru – Vayu’s brothers.

sentences.en: “Oh, as you know, I had sold Vayu to you some years back.
sentences.zh: “哦，如你所知，几年前我就把 Vayu 卖给了你。

sentences.en: Yesterday I was passing by your village early in the morning in my buggy pulled by Jhabru and Ghabru – Vayu’s brothers.
sentences.zh: 昨天一大早，我乘坐由瓦尤（Vayu）兄弟贾布鲁（Jhabru）和加布鲁（Ghabru）拉的马车路过你们的村庄。

picturePages.text: I don’t know how Vayu got loose and followed us back to Chandesara!

sentences.en: I don’t know how Vayu got loose and followed us back to Chandesara!
sentences.zh: 我不知道 Vayu 是怎么逃脱并跟着我们回到 Chandesara 的！

stories.title: Technoblade: The Potato War
stories.synopsis: 土豆种植怎么变成了一场策略大战？
paragraphs: What kind of battle can you fight with potatoes? Technoblade was a real Minecraft player. He made videos, played games, and told funny stories. In one of his best-known challenges, an ordinary crop became the heart of a long contest.

His rival was another player, Im_a_Squid_Kid. Their contest became known as the Potato War. It lasted for months. Growing more potatoes sounds simple. But a long contest raises a harder question: how can you keep improving when someone else is trying to beat you?

Technoblade was known for both skill and humor. He could tell the story of a game as if it were a great battle. The Potato War brought these two sides together: serious competition and funny storytelling. That mixture helped make the contest memorable.

A small goal can lead to a big story. Think about the contest. Which matters most to you: winning, finding a clever method, or making something people enjoy? Could a person lose a contest and still create a story worth remembering?

stories.title: The Magic Powder - A Folktale from Myanmar
stories.synopsis: 泥土能变成黄金吗？一场有关梦想与计谋的较量。
paragraphs: Once upon a time, in a little village on the banks of the Irrawaddy river, there lived a young woman called Thuza. She was very happily married to handsome young Theingi.
But there was one problem that nagged Thuza – her husband believed he was an alchemist and would spend all his time dreaming about ways to turn dirt into gold.
All day, and for days on end, Theingi spent his time in experiments, searching for a breakthrough.

Soon, all their money was over, and young Thuza had to struggle to buy food for the two of them. She became very worried. “You should find a job soon,” she pleaded with her husband. “We cannot continue like this!” But Theingi wouldn’t listen.
“I’m on the verge of a breakthrough!

Why do I have to work when we will be rich beyond our wildest dreams? We will soon be able to turn all the dirt we find into gold!” Disheartened, Thuza approached her father, wise old Thet, for a solution.
Thet was surprised when he heard that his son-in-law was an alchemist.
He thought for a while and asked to see Theingi. Thuza returned home happily that day, for she knew her wise father would have a solution.

The next day, Theingi arrived at his father-in-law’s house, fully prepared for a scolding. He was taken by surprise when Thet took him aside and whispered, “When I was young like you, I was an alchemist too!”
The two of them spent the whole afternoon discussing Theingi’s work.

Finally, the old man stood up and said, “Why Theingi, you’ve done everything exactly like I did when I was your age! You are definitely on the verge of a breakthrough! Congratulations! But you seem to be lacking one very important ingredient in your experiments.
You will need this when you finally turn dirt to gold.
Only recently did I discover this. But I am too old for this task. It requires enormous effort … ” “Then let me do it for you, Father!” cried Theingi. He was really excited.
All his efforts would pay off at last. “Tell me what the ingredient is!” “Good, you are excited!” said Thet.
He leaned closer and whispered, “Son, the secret ingredient is a silver powder that is found only on banana leaves. You will have to plant the bananas yourself and cast certain spells on them.
Then, as the plants grow, the powder on the leaves will gain magical powers.”
“How much of this powder will we need, Father?” asked Theingi excitedly. “A kilo,” replied Thet. “A kilo!” cried Theingi.
“That would require hundreds of banana plants!” “I’m afraid so, Son,” said the old man. “That is why I can’t complete the task myself … ” “Don’t lose heart, Father!” said Theingi. “I shall!”
Later that evening, the old man taught his son-in-law the magic spells and loaned him the money to start the work. The very next day, Theingi bought a small field near his home and cleared it.
Just as he had been instructed, he dug the ground himself and planted the saplings after carefully chanting the magic spells.

Every day he went to the field and examined the saplings. He kept the weeds and pests away diligently. When the plants grew and bore fruit, he carefully collected the silver powder from the leaves and kept it safely in a box.
There was hardly any powder on each leaf, so Theingi had to buy more land and grow more bananas. But he was determined to do what was needed.
It took him several years, but at the end of it all, he had managed to collect enough of the magic powder. He rushed to his father-in-law, excited as never before.
He would soon be able to make gold from mere dirt! “Father, finally … here is the kilo of magic powder!” he cried. The old man was filled with joy. “Wonderful!’’ he said.
“Wonderful! You’ve done well, Theingi. I’m proud of you. Now I will show you how to turn dirt into gold. But first, let’s get Thuza.

We need her help.” Theingi was a little puzzled, but without losing any time, he ran to his wife and was soon back with her. “Thuza,” asked the old man, “what did you do with the bananas when your husband was collecting the powder?”
“Why, I sold them, Father,” replied Thuza. “That’s how we earned a living.”
“Then you must have been able to save some money too. Theingi grew more than enough bananas … ” the old man continued. “Yes, I did,” replied Thuza. “Can we see it?” asked Thet.
“Of course, I have kept it safely at home,” beamed Thuza.

The three of them went to Theingi’s house where Thuza produced several bags from the loft where she had kept them safely. Thet opened one of the bags, peered inside, and smiled. He then emptied one of the bags on the table.
Gold coins tinkled as they fell in a huge, shiny heap.
Then he went to the field and came back with a handful of dirt, which he placed next to the heap of gold. “You see, Theingi,” he said, turning to his son-in-law, “you have changed dirt into gold!”
Never after that day did Theingi collect any more magic powder from the leaves. But he continued to grow bananas.
His “alchemist” father-in-law had taught him the best way to turn dirt into gold, after all. He didn’t need the magic powder any more.

BANANAGIC! After Theingi’s magic powder from bananas, how about surprising your friends with some magical bananas?! Tell them about a new variety that you have just discovered – one that grows in slices!
MAKE YOUR OWN MAGICAL BANANAS YOU’LL NEED: A few ripe bananas A toothpick or sewing needle
HOW TO MAKE IT: 1. Push the toothpick into the banana somewhere along the seam. 2. Without taking it out, carefully rotate the toothpick left and right inside the banana.
You should cut all the way through the fruit, but not through the peel, mind you.
Also, try and keep the toothpick hole as small as possible – the smaller, the lesser it will be visible.

3. Remove the toothpick and repeat the above step at another spot on the banana, say after an inch. Keep making internal one-inch slices until you have at least five or six. Do these two steps with all the bananas you have.
That’s it – your magic bananas are ready to eat.

Offer the “new variety” to your friends while telling them a big story about how you discovered them in the field nearby. When your friends peel the banana, imagine the look on their faces when they find that it is already sliced?
While inside the skin! Isn’t that some yummy banana magic?

stories.title: Jadav and the Tree-Place
stories.synopsis: 一个人、一片荒地，和几十年种树的日子。
paragraphs: This is Jadav, a tree-planter. He loves tree-places because they are full of life. No-tree-places make him terribly sad, because they are full of dead things.
Years ago, Jadav was walking along the banks of the great Brahmaputra River when he arrived at a big, empty no- tree-place. It was dry and hot. The sand was powdery and striped.
Striped sand? How odd. Jadav went closer to take a better look. Oh, but they weren't stripes at all! The ground was covered in snakes!
Last night’s floods must have washed them ashore, Jadav thought.

These snakes weren't slinking and slithering and swaying about like regular, healthy snakes. When Jadav walked among them, they didn't hiss or run away or try to bite him. They just lay about like old ropes, tired and still. "Poor snakes!
They're dying from the heat! If only they had some shade to lie in!
If only this no-tree-place had some trees in it!"
Jadav couldn't bear to watch the snakes die. It made him so terribly sad that he sat down and began to cry. But he quickly came to his senses. "No more crying. From now on: only trying!"
He jumped up, ran back to his village and began collecting all the bamboo shoots he could carry in his bag.
"Regular plants won't grow in the hot sand, but bamboo will. Bamboo is strong!"

Jadav brought the shoots to the no-tree-place and started planting them everywhere. It was hard, hot work, and it took years. The river grew thin one summer and flooded the next, sometimes bringing more sand and sometimes taking it away. Heavy rains came and went.
But Jadav kept on planting.

In time, the bamboo took root and began to grow. As it grew, it brought shade, and the shade brought insects. The insects burrowed into the ground, and the earth below the bamboo trees began to change.
The dry and white became rich and brown, and the dead sand became living soil.

Jadav was no longer sad. But he wasn't happy either. He looked around his bamboo grove and thought, "A few-trees-place is nice, I know. But how wonderful it would be if this were a many-trees-place!" The idea thrilled him.
So Jadav went back to his village and began collecting many more seeds and saplings.
He filled three big bags with Arjun and ejar and gulmohar and koroi and moj and himolu. "Now that our few-trees-place has lovely brown soil, we can plant all these and more!"

Jadav brought his new saplings and seeds to the few-trees-place and planted them all around. It was hard work, his back hurt, and it took many years. The orange and blue skies turned purple and pink, and villages became towns.
The wind grew laden with dust, and the river became grey.
But Jadav's insect friends helped to till the soil, and his tall bamboos gave him shade and cooled the air. And Jadav kept on planting.

Soon, his Arjun, ejar and gulmohar, his koroi, moj and himolu, and all his many other plants dug in, took root and started growing. As they grew, they spread new seeds, and the new seeds, in turn, took root.
Shoots became trunks, trunks grew branches, and the branches reached for the sky.
The few-trees-place that was once a no-tree-place now became a wonderful, green many-trees-place. But what's a many-trees-place without many tree-creatures? When one came, the others followed.

First, came the birds. They flocked and flew in from near and far, to make their nests in Jadav's tree-place. There were vultures and pelicans and storks and ducks. And warblers and thrushes and wagtails and chats.

Next, came the animals. They skipped and swung and sauntered in, to make their homes in the many-trees-place. There were buffaloes and deer and rabbits and gibbons. And elephants and tigers and rhinos.

Finally, there came the snakes. They slithered and swayed and sashayed in, to cool themselves in the shade of Jadav's trees. When Jadav saw the snakes, he sat down and cried happy tears. He was so happy that he wasn't even afraid of getting bitten.

Jadav's tree-place had filled with feathers and beaks and wings, with claws and tails and fangs. There were spots and splashes, stripes and flashes, and green, green, everywhere. The tree-place was a forest, at last. And Jadav was a happy man.

Then Jadav had another thought. "Many trees in one place is good, I know. But how wonderful it'd be if there were many trees in every place!" So he grabbed his bags of seeds and started walking across the world.
And as he walked, Jadav started planting the seeds in all the no-tree-places he saw. And he planted. And planted.
And planted. But there are so many no-tree-places in the world. There are more no-tree-places than tree-places now. This is terribly sad, but Jadav does not sit down and cry this time.
Jadav plants.
And plants. And plants some more.

It’s going to be hard work, bringing all the old forests back. The seas have begun rising, and the winds grow cold. Towns have become cities, and Jadav is growing old. But he keeps on planting. And planting.
And planting.
Jadav will keep on planting until the whole world is a happy, lovely lots-of-trees-place.
Jadav in Real Life Jadav ‘Mulai’ Payeng is a conservationist and recipient of the Padmashree, one of the highest civilian honours awarded by the Indian government. Jadav lives in Majuli, Assam.

At the age of 16, distressed by the sight of dying snakes that had washed up on a sandbar banking the Brahmaputra, Jadav decided to plant some trees in the spot. He started small, with bamboos, and grew an entire forest, plant by painstaking plant.
This was back in 1979.
Over the next three decades, Jadav and his tree- planting have managed to change the soil in the barren area.
The 550-hectare sandbar is now a lush, dense forest and home to a variety of flora and fauna, including elephants, tigers, apes, deer and many species of local and migratory birds.
Jadav continues to visit and nurture his forest every day, planting wherever he finds empty patches.
Growing Up With a Mango Tree: a Tree-Planting Activity Just ate a mango? Loved it? Want another? You can go to a shop and buy one, of course.
But it's a lot more fun (and free!) to use the seed of the mango you just ate and make a few fruits of your own.
All you need is time and patience. First, find a nice patch of empty land near your house. Get a friend, sibling or grown-up to help you plant the seed you saved in that patch.
Make sure the soil is loose and there's plenty of sun.
It may take several weeks of waiting, watering and watching before your seed turns into a plant, so don't worry and definitely don't hurry.

Once your seed germinates and grows into a healthy mango plant, get ready for a lot more waiting, watering and watching. Take care that your plant doesn't get eaten up by insects or animals, or get stepped on by someone.
If all this waiting is making you feel bored, read a few books, sing some songs, and plant some more plants!
After a few years, as you grow taller, your mango plant will grow tall with you, until it becomes a big tree that you can climb and picnic under. This is when the real fun begins.

By now, your tree will have started making its own mangoes, which you and your friends can eat. Even better, those mangoes will soon start attracting other mango- loving creatures to your tree: birds, ants, squirrels, bats, monkeys, spiders and lots more.

Some of these creatures will come to eat the fruit, some will come to feed on the tree's sap, some to drink nectar from its flowers, and some creatures will even come to eat some of the other creatures hanging around the tree.
But it's not all about eating.
Some creatures may come just to rest in your tree's shade, or to take a nap in its branches. Your tree has many different uses for every different creature!
Spend some time every day watching who visits your mango tree, at which time of the day they come, and what they do. Write down what you see in your notebook.

Also draw pictures of what you see. See how much you've done and learned with just one mango seed? Isn't tree-planting fun? Now imagine how much fun Jadav must have had planting his entire forest full of trees!

picturePages.text: In time, the bamboo took root and began to grow. As it grew, it brought shade, and the shade brought insects. The insects burrowed into the ground, and the earth below the bamboo trees began to change.

sentences.en: In time, the bamboo took root and began to grow.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，竹子生根发芽，开始生长。

sentences.en: As it grew, it brought shade, and the shade brought insects.
sentences.zh: 随着它的生长，它带来了阴凉，阴凉又带来了昆虫。

sentences.en: The insects burrowed into the ground, and the earth below the bamboo trees began to change.
sentences.zh: 虫子钻入地下，竹树下的大地开始发生变化。

picturePages.text: The dry and white became rich and brown, and the dead sand became living soil.

sentences.en: The dry and white became rich and brown, and the dead sand became living soil.
sentences.zh: 干燥的白色变成了浓郁的棕色，死沙变成了活土。

picturePages.text: Jadav was no longer sad. But he wasn't happy either. He looked around his bamboo grove and thought, "A few-trees-place is nice, I know. But how wonderful it would be if this were a many-trees-place!" The idea thrilled him.

sentences.en: Jadav was no longer sad.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫不再悲伤。

sentences.en: But he wasn't happy either.
sentences.zh: 但他也不高兴。

sentences.en: He looked around his bamboo grove and thought, "A few-trees-place is nice, I know.
sentences.zh: 他环顾四周的竹林，心想：“我知道，有几棵树的地方很好。

sentences.en: But how wonderful it would be if this were a many-trees-place!"
sentences.zh: 但如果这是一个有很多树的地方该多好啊！”

sentences.en: The idea thrilled him.
sentences.zh: 这个想法让他兴奋不已。

picturePages.text: So Jadav went back to his village and began collecting many more seeds and saplings.

sentences.en: So Jadav went back to his village and began collecting many more seeds and saplings.
sentences.zh: 于是贾达夫回到了他的村庄，开始收集更多的种子和树苗。

picturePages.text: He filled three big bags with Arjun and ejar and gulmohar and koroi and moj and himolu. "Now that our few-trees-place has lovely brown soil, we can plant all these and more!"

sentences.en: He filled three big bags with Arjun and ejar and gulmohar and koroi and moj and himolu.
sentences.zh: 他装满了三个大袋子，里面装着阿琼、埃贾尔、古尔莫哈尔、科罗伊、莫杰和希莫鲁。

sentences.en: "Now that our few-trees-place has lovely brown soil, we can plant all these and more!"
sentences.zh: “现在我们的几棵树已经有了可爱的棕色土壤，我们可以种植所有这些以及更多！”

picturePages.text: Jadav brought his new saplings and seeds to the few-trees-place and planted them all around. It was hard work, his back hurt, and it took many years. The orange and blue skies turned purple and pink, and villages became towns.

sentences.en: Jadav brought his new saplings and seeds to the few-trees-place and planted them all around.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫把他的新树苗和种子带到了树木稀少的地方，并将它们种植在周围。

sentences.en: It was hard work, his back hurt, and it took many years.
sentences.zh: 这是一项艰苦的工作，他的背很痛，而且花了很多年的时间。

sentences.en: The orange and blue skies turned purple and pink, and villages became towns.
sentences.zh: 橙色和蓝色的天空变成了紫色和粉色，村庄变成了城镇。

picturePages.text: The wind grew laden with dust, and the river became grey.

sentences.en: The wind grew laden with dust, and the river became grey.
sentences.zh: 风中夹杂着灰尘，河水变成了灰色。

picturePages.text: But Jadav's insect friends helped to till the soil, and his tall bamboos gave him shade and cooled the air. And Jadav kept on planting.

sentences.en: But Jadav's insect friends helped to till the soil, and his tall bamboos gave him shade and cooled the air.
sentences.zh: 但贾达夫的昆虫朋友帮助耕耘土壤，高大的竹子为他提供阴凉并冷却空气。

sentences.en: And Jadav kept on planting.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫继续种植。

picturePages.text: Soon, his Arjun, ejar and gulmohar, his koroi, moj and himolu, and all his many other plants dug in, took root and started growing. As they grew, they spread new seeds, and the new seeds, in turn, took root.

sentences.en: Soon, his Arjun, ejar and gulmohar, his koroi, moj and himolu, and all his many other plants dug in, took root and started growing.
sentences.zh: 很快，他的 Arjun、ejar 和 gulmohar，他的 koroi、moj 和 Himolu，以及所有其他植物都在其中扎根并开始生长。

sentences.en: As they grew, they spread new seeds, and the new seeds, in turn, took root.
sentences.zh: 随着它们的成长，它们传播新的种子，而新的种子又生根发芽。

picturePages.text: Shoots became trunks, trunks grew branches, and the branches reached for the sky.

sentences.en: Shoots became trunks, trunks grew branches, and the branches reached for the sky.
sentences.zh: 嫩芽变成树干，树干长出枝条，枝条伸向天空。

picturePages.text: The few-trees-place that was once a no-tree-place now became a wonderful, green many-trees-place. But what's a many-trees-place without many tree-creatures? When one came, the others followed.

sentences.en: The few-trees-place that was once a no-tree-place now became a wonderful, green many-trees-place.
sentences.zh: 曾经没有树的地方现在变成了一个美丽的、绿色的、多树的地方。

sentences.en: But what's a many-trees-place without many tree-creatures?
sentences.zh: 但是，一个有很多树的地方怎么能没有很多树生物呢？

sentences.en: When one came, the others followed.
sentences.zh: 一人来了，其他人也跟着来了。

picturePages.text: First, came the birds. They flocked and flew in from near and far, to make their nests in Jadav's tree-place. There were vultures and pelicans and storks and ducks. And warblers and thrushes and wagtails and chats.

sentences.en: First, came the birds.
sentences.zh: 首先是鸟儿来了。

sentences.en: They flocked and flew in from near and far, to make their nests in Jadav's tree-place.
sentences.zh: 它们成群结队地从远近飞来，在贾达夫的树上筑巢。

sentences.en: There were vultures and pelicans and storks and ducks.
sentences.zh: 有秃鹰、鹈鹕、鹳和鸭子。

sentences.en: And warblers and thrushes and wagtails and chats.
sentences.zh: 还有莺、画眉、鹡鸰和聊天。

picturePages.text: Next, came the animals. They skipped and swung and sauntered in, to make their homes in the many-trees-place. There were buffaloes and deer and rabbits and gibbons. And elephants and tigers and rhinos.

sentences.en: Next, came the animals.
sentences.zh: 接下来，动物们来了。

sentences.en: They skipped and swung and sauntered in, to make their homes in the many-trees-place.
sentences.zh: 他们蹦蹦跳跳、晃晃悠悠地走进来，在树木繁茂的地方安家。

sentences.en: There were buffaloes and deer and rabbits and gibbons.
sentences.zh: 有水牛、鹿、兔子和长臂猿。

sentences.en: And elephants and tigers and rhinos.
sentences.zh: 还有大象、老虎和犀牛。

picturePages.text: Finally, there came the snakes. They slithered and swayed and sashayed in, to cool themselves in the shade of Jadav's trees. When Jadav saw the snakes, he sat down and cried happy tears. He was so happy that he wasn't even afraid of getting bitten.

sentences.en: Finally, there came the snakes.
sentences.zh: 最后，蛇来了。

sentences.en: They slithered and swayed and sashayed in, to cool themselves in the shade of Jadav's trees.
sentences.zh: 他们滑行、摇摆、大摇大摆地进去，在贾达夫的树荫下纳凉。

sentences.en: When Jadav saw the snakes, he sat down and cried happy tears.
sentences.zh: 当贾达夫看到蛇时，他坐下来，流下了幸福的泪水。

sentences.en: He was so happy that he wasn't even afraid of getting bitten.
sentences.zh: 他高兴极了，连被咬都不怕了。

picturePages.text: Jadav's tree-place had filled with feathers and beaks and wings, with claws and tails and fangs. There were spots and splashes, stripes and flashes, and green, green, everywhere. The tree-place was a forest, at last. And Jadav was a happy man.

sentences.en: Jadav's tree-place had filled with feathers and beaks and wings, with claws and tails and fangs.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫的树上长满了羽毛、喙和翅膀，还有爪子、尾巴和尖牙。

sentences.en: There were spots and splashes, stripes and flashes, and green, green, everywhere.
sentences.zh: 到处都是斑点和飞溅，条纹和闪光，绿色，绿色，到处都是。

sentences.en: The tree-place was a forest, at last.
sentences.zh: 树所在的地方终于变成了森林。

sentences.en: And Jadav was a happy man.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫是一个快乐的人。

picturePages.text: Then Jadav had another thought. "Many trees in one place is good, I know. But how wonderful it'd be if there were many trees in every place!" So he grabbed his bags of seeds and started walking across the world.

sentences.en: Then Jadav had another thought.
sentences.zh: 然后贾达夫有了另一个想法。

sentences.en: "Many trees in one place is good, I know.
sentences.zh: “我知道，一处多棵树是好事。

sentences.en: But how wonderful it'd be if there were many trees in every place!"
sentences.zh: 但如果每个地方都有很多树该多好啊！”

sentences.en: So he grabbed his bags of seeds and started walking across the world.
sentences.zh: 于是，他拿起一袋袋种子，开始徒步穿越世界。

picturePages.text: And as he walked, Jadav started planting the seeds in all the no-tree-places he saw. And he planted. And planted.

sentences.en: And as he walked, Jadav started planting the seeds in all the no-tree-places he saw.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫边走边开始在他看到的所有没有树的地方播种种子。

sentences.en: And he planted.
sentences.zh: 他种植了。

sentences.en: And planted.
sentences.zh: 并种植。

picturePages.text: And planted. But there are so many no-tree-places in the world. There are more no-tree-places than tree-places now. This is terribly sad, but Jadav does not sit down and cry this time.

sentences.en: And planted.
sentences.zh: 并种植。

sentences.en: But there are so many no-tree-places in the world.
sentences.zh: 但世界上有很多没有树的地方。

sentences.en: There are more no-tree-places than tree-places now.
sentences.zh: 现在无树的地方比有树的地方多。

sentences.en: This is terribly sad, but Jadav does not sit down and cry this time.
sentences.zh: 这真是太悲伤了，但贾达夫这次没有坐下来哭泣。

picturePages.text: Jadav plants.

sentences.en: Jadav plants.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫植物。

picturePages.text: And plants. And plants some more.

sentences.en: And plants.
sentences.zh: 还有植物。

sentences.en: And plants some more.
sentences.zh: 还种了一些。

picturePages.text: It’s going to be hard work, bringing all the old forests back. The seas have begun rising, and the winds grow cold. Towns have become cities, and Jadav is growing old. But he keeps on planting. And planting.

sentences.en: It’s going to be hard work, bringing all the old forests back.
sentences.zh: 恢复所有古老的森林将是一项艰苦的工作。

sentences.en: The seas have begun rising, and the winds grow cold.
sentences.zh: 海平面开始上升，风也变得寒冷。

sentences.en: Towns have become cities, and Jadav is growing old.
sentences.zh: 城镇变成了城市，贾达夫也日渐老去。

sentences.en: But he keeps on planting.
sentences.zh: 但他仍继续种植。

sentences.en: And planting.
sentences.zh: 并种植。

picturePages.text: And planting.

sentences.en: And planting.
sentences.zh: 并种植。

picturePages.text: Jadav will keep on planting until the whole world is a happy, lovely lots-of-trees-place.

sentences.en: Jadav will keep on planting until the whole world is a happy, lovely lots-of-trees-place.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫将继续种植，直到整个世界成为一个快乐、可爱、树木繁茂的地方。

picturePages.text: Jadav in Real Life Jadav ‘Mulai’ Payeng is a conservationist and recipient of the Padmashree, one of the highest civilian honours awarded by the Indian government. Jadav lives in Majuli, Assam.

sentences.en: Jadav in Real Life Jadav ‘Mulai’ Payeng is a conservationist and recipient of the Padmashree, one of the highest civilian honours awarded by the Indian government.
sentences.zh: 现实生活中的 Jadav Jadav ‘Mulai’ Payeng 是一位自然资源保护主义者，也是印度政府授予的最高平民荣誉之一的莲花士勋章获得者。

sentences.en: Jadav lives in Majuli, Assam.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫住在阿萨姆邦马朱利。

picturePages.text: At the age of 16, distressed by the sight of dying snakes that had washed up on a sandbar banking the Brahmaputra, Jadav decided to plant some trees in the spot. He started small, with bamboos, and grew an entire forest, plant by painstaking plant.

sentences.en: At the age of 16, distressed by the sight of dying snakes that had washed up on a sandbar banking the Brahmaputra, Jadav decided to plant some trees in the spot.
sentences.zh: 16 岁时，贾达夫看到雅鲁藏布江沿岸的沙洲上有一条条垂死的蛇被冲上岸，他感到十分痛苦，于是他决定在该地种植一些树。

sentences.en: He started small, with bamboos, and grew an entire forest, plant by painstaking plant.
sentences.zh: 他从小处开始，用竹子开始种植整个森林，一棵又一棵地繁衍生息。

picturePages.text: This was back in 1979.

sentences.en: This was back in 1979.
sentences.zh: 这已经是 1979 年的事了。

picturePages.text: Over the next three decades, Jadav and his tree- planting have managed to change the soil in the barren area.

sentences.en: Over the next three decades, Jadav and his tree- planting have managed to change the soil in the barren area.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的三十年里，贾达夫和他的植树活动成功地改变了贫瘠地区的土壤。

picturePages.text: The 550-hectare sandbar is now a lush, dense forest and home to a variety of flora and fauna, including elephants, tigers, apes, deer and many species of local and migratory birds.

sentences.en: The 550-hectare sandbar is now a lush, dense forest and home to a variety of flora and fauna, including elephants, tigers, apes, deer and many species of local and migratory birds.
sentences.zh: 这片占地 550 公顷的沙洲现在是一片郁郁葱葱的茂密森林，是各种动植物的家园，包括大象、老虎、猿、鹿以及多种当地鸟类和候鸟。

picturePages.text: Jadav continues to visit and nurture his forest every day, planting wherever he finds empty patches.

sentences.en: Jadav continues to visit and nurture his forest every day, planting wherever he finds empty patches.
sentences.zh: 贾达夫每天继续参观和培育他的森林，在发现空地的地方进行种植。

picturePages.text: Growing Up With a Mango Tree: a Tree-Planting Activity Just ate a mango? Loved it? Want another? You can go to a shop and buy one, of course.

sentences.en: Growing Up With a Mango Tree: a Tree-Planting Activity Just ate a mango?
sentences.zh: 与芒果树一起成长：植树活动 刚吃了一个芒果？

sentences.en: Loved it?
sentences.zh: 喜欢它吗？

sentences.en: Want another?
sentences.zh: 想要另一个吗？

sentences.en: You can go to a shop and buy one, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，您可以去商店买一个。

picturePages.text: But it's a lot more fun (and free!) to use the seed of the mango you just ate and make a few fruits of your own.

sentences.en: But it's a lot more fun (and free!) to use the seed of the mango you just ate and make a few fruits of your own.
sentences.zh: 但是，使用您刚刚吃的芒果种子并自己制作一些水果会更有趣（而且免费！）。

picturePages.text: All you need is time and patience. First, find a nice patch of empty land near your house. Get a friend, sibling or grown-up to help you plant the seed you saved in that patch.

sentences.en: All you need is time and patience.
sentences.zh: 您所需要的只是时间和耐心。

sentences.en: First, find a nice patch of empty land near your house.
sentences.zh: 首先，在你家附近找到一块漂亮的空地。

sentences.en: Get a friend, sibling or grown-up to help you plant the seed you saved in that patch.
sentences.zh: 找一个朋友、兄弟姐妹或成年人来帮助你种下你在那片土地上保存的种子。

picturePages.text: Make sure the soil is loose and there's plenty of sun.

sentences.en: Make sure the soil is loose and there's plenty of sun.
sentences.zh: 确保土壤疏松并且有充足的阳光。

picturePages.text: It may take several weeks of waiting, watering and watching before your seed turns into a plant, so don't worry and definitely don't hurry.

sentences.en: It may take several weeks of waiting, watering and watching before your seed turns into a plant, so don't worry and definitely don't hurry.
sentences.zh: 在你的种子长成植物之前，可能需要几周的等待、浇水和观察，所以不要担心，也不要着急。

picturePages.text: Once your seed germinates and grows into a healthy mango plant, get ready for a lot more waiting, watering and watching. Take care that your plant doesn't get eaten up by insects or animals, or get stepped on by someone.

sentences.en: Once your seed germinates and grows into a healthy mango plant, get ready for a lot more waiting, watering and watching.
sentences.zh: 一旦你的种子发芽并长成健康的芒果植株，准备好接受更多的等待、浇水和观察。

sentences.en: Take care that your plant doesn't get eaten up by insects or animals, or get stepped on by someone.
sentences.zh: 小心你的植物不要被昆虫或动物吃掉，或者被人踩到。

picturePages.text: If all this waiting is making you feel bored, read a few books, sing some songs, and plant some more plants!

sentences.en: If all this waiting is making you feel bored, read a few books, sing some songs, and plant some more plants!
sentences.zh: 如果所有的等待让你感到无聊，那就读几本书，唱一些歌，多种植一些植物吧！

picturePages.text: After a few years, as you grow taller, your mango plant will grow tall with you, until it becomes a big tree that you can climb and picnic under. This is when the real fun begins.

sentences.en: After a few years, as you grow taller, your mango plant will grow tall with you, until it becomes a big tree that you can climb and picnic under.
sentences.zh: 几年后，随着你长高，你的芒果树也会跟着你一起长高，直到它变成一棵大树，你可以爬到树下野餐。

sentences.en: This is when the real fun begins.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正的乐趣开始的时候。

picturePages.text: By now, your tree will have started making its own mangoes, which you and your friends can eat. Even better, those mangoes will soon start attracting other mango- loving creatures to your tree: birds, ants, squirrels, bats, monkeys, spiders and lots more.

sentences.en: By now, your tree will have started making its own mangoes, which you and your friends can eat.
sentences.zh: 现在，您的树将开始生产自己的芒果，您和您的朋友可以吃它们。

sentences.en: Even better, those mangoes will soon start attracting other mango- loving creatures to your tree: birds, ants, squirrels, bats, monkeys, spiders and lots more.
sentences.zh: 更好的是，这些芒果很快就会开始吸引其他喜欢芒果的生物到你的树上：鸟类、蚂蚁、松鼠、蝙蝠、猴子、蜘蛛等等。

picturePages.text: Some of these creatures will come to eat the fruit, some will come to feed on the tree's sap, some to drink nectar from its flowers, and some creatures will even come to eat some of the other creatures hanging around the tree.

sentences.en: Some of these creatures will come to eat the fruit, some will come to feed on the tree's sap, some to drink nectar from its flowers, and some creatures will even come to eat some of the other creatures hanging around the tree.
sentences.zh: 其中一些生物会来吃果实，一些会来吃树的汁液，一些会来喝花中的花蜜，有些生物甚至会来吃树周围的其他一些生物。

picturePages.text: But it's not all about eating.

sentences.en: But it's not all about eating.
sentences.zh: 但这不仅仅与吃有关。

picturePages.text: Some creatures may come just to rest in your tree's shade, or to take a nap in its branches. Your tree has many different uses for every different creature!

sentences.en: Some creatures may come just to rest in your tree's shade, or to take a nap in its branches.
sentences.zh: 有些生物可能只是来你的树荫下休息，或者在树枝上小憩。

sentences.en: Your tree has many different uses for every different creature!
sentences.zh: 您的树对每种不同的生物都有许多不同的用途！

picturePages.text: Spend some time every day watching who visits your mango tree, at which time of the day they come, and what they do. Write down what you see in your notebook.

sentences.en: Spend some time every day watching who visits your mango tree, at which time of the day they come, and what they do.
sentences.zh: 每天花一些时间观察谁参观你的芒果树、他们在一天中的什么时间来以及他们做了什么。

sentences.en: Write down what you see in your notebook.
sentences.zh: 写下你在笔记本上看到的内容。

picturePages.text: Also draw pictures of what you see. See how much you've done and learned with just one mango seed? Isn't tree-planting fun? Now imagine how much fun Jadav must have had planting his entire forest full of trees!

sentences.en: Also draw pictures of what you see.
sentences.zh: 还可以画出你所看到的图片。

sentences.en: See how much you've done and learned with just one mango seed?
sentences.zh: 看看您仅用一颗芒果种子就完成了多少工作并学到了多少知识？

sentences.en: Isn't tree-planting fun?
sentences.zh: 植树不是很有趣吗？

sentences.en: Now imagine how much fun Jadav must have had planting his entire forest full of trees!
sentences.zh: 现在想象一下贾达夫在他的整个森林中种满了树木一定有多么有趣！

stories.title: Philza: A Five-Year World
stories.synopsis: 花五年建造的世界，突然结束了。这五年还值不值得？
paragraphs: Philza spent five years playing in one Minecraft Hardcore world. He built a large, complex world and shared his play on Twitch. A game session can last an hour. His adventure lasted years. Every new day added something to the world he had made.

Then, during a live stream, his character died. A baby zombie in gold armor and a spider ended the run. Philza was safe in real life. It was his character who died. But five years of surviving in that world had come to an end.

The news spread beyond his own viewers. Newspapers and people on social media discussed what had happened. Minecraft's official website shared his story too. A failure in a game had become a story that many people wanted to understand.

Was that time wasted? A game can end, but the player can still remember the work. Think about something you built or learned. If you lost the finished thing, what would remain: your skills, your memories, or the people who shared the journey?
